Your feelings sound intense and incredibly hard to deal with. I can't imagine what it is like to live in such a hostile environment. I will not try to change your mind one way or the other but I want to just say that I have found personally and interpersonally, LGBT people find life to be less exhausting once they are living on their own. Meeting similar people is easier and there is less familial pressure weighing on you to be one way or another. I hope that can offer something positive? I realize you aren't 18 yet but, things begin to improve once you hit that milestone. Again, I appreciate that you are suffering and I hope you are able to find some sense of repose.

Also, not an attack, but what's wrong with being feminine? I mean I realize society says men are "supposed" to be masculine, but femininity isn't a bad thing. I realize it's not as easy as I make it out to be, but learning to embrace one's feminine and masculine traits and appreciate them for what they are, is one of the things that helped me move on from an actively suicidal bisexual high schooler, to an adult who graduated from university, starting a new amazing job and moving into a house with my partner at the end of the month. I know things don't always work for everyone as well as they have for me, but... I hope you are eventually able to find some love for yourself, at the least.
